proposedContributions.change: Implement the CI-001-approved CodeSearchProvider search/read/status/reindex contract. Obtain current CI-002 caller authorization and immutable snapshot before selecting a backend. Text mode calls source-index-facade.searchSourceIndex; literal/regex modes use a capability-pinned rg executable via spawn(executable, argv, { shell: false }) with bounded stdout/stderr and cancellation. Build spans from verified snapshot file bytes, never from normalized FTS snippets. Read resolves the same immutable span with current policy and reports freshness separately. Status and reindex delegate to index-status.ts and the existing facade; do not open another index or execute repository hooks.
proposedContributions.interfacePrerequisite: Exact request/result/error schemas and rg capability injection contract require accepted CI-001/CI-002 receipts. Proposed names here are contributions, not claims of existing symbols.

proposedContributions.change: Project facade-owned index metadata into SearchIndex: binding/snapshot identity, policy fingerprint, actual backend/version, indexed/skipped counts, per-file and aggregate coverage, limits, build time, stale/unavailable reason and index revision. Reindex authorized immutable snapshot content through the facade under the existing workspace index writer; never clear unrelated source rows. Read durable coverage from the same facade-owned DB after restart. A missing metadata receipt is unknown coverage, not complete coverage.

Use deterministic temporary corpora and the real provider path for positive/absent matches, injection-like and dash-prefixed literals, rg invalid regex, result/output/time limits, actual process cancellation, SQLite unavailable versus true zero matches, exact SHA-256 and 1-based spans including Unicode/CRLF, stale source and current-policy denial, shared-index preservation and coverage readback after reopen. Follow the existing bun:test and closeAllSourceIndexes cleanup pattern. Do not claim existing source tests cover new behavior.

foundationGates.gate: Lead wave0 commit, accepted dependency artifact plus authoritative readback receipts, assigned implementation owner and exclusive leases for all shared paths. Resolve reference package revision/digest from delivery manifest; reconcile historical product_baseline_sha e953786ba7e30fb5da5dca7e88e20e324d5aebab with approved prerequisite commits rather than silently using dirty a21aeab input.

EG-IDENTITY and CI scoped repository/egress policy need real actor/workspace readiness receipts. Existing immutable scope checks are not live actor lookup or offline lease enforcement. The accepted CI-002 shared resolver must authorize before rg/FTS and again on read; remote-private offline is denied by default, expiry/reconnect invalidate access, and any signed lease records the disconnected revocation exposure window.

The inspected CodeIntelligenceProvider describes operations and registry metadata but defines no search/read/status/reindex methods or search error schemas; CodeIntelAdapter is still synchronous symbols-only. Request precise canonical contract additions from CI-001 before implementation; do not establish a parallel provider interface in CI-003. indexVerifiedSnapshotFiles currently excludes dirty files without commitSha, so dirty search and symbol provenance must not silently disappear or cite a parent commit.

Verify actual rg executable/version/license/readiness and a read-only exact-snapshot execution strategy. Running rg on a mutable canonicalRoot alone cannot search historical snapshot bytes. Use the accepted snapshot materialization mechanism if available; otherwise implement bounded request-local materialization of approved snapshot files under the existing temporary-artifact policy, removed on completion/cancel, not a persistent second store. Do not install/probe rg during preflight.

The facade has no AbortSignal/deadline option; TS SQLite queries are synchronous and a Promise wrapper is not preemptive cancellation. Native calls also lack cancellation parameters at this seam. Integration owner must supply a demonstrably bounded facade execution/cancellation path and preserve native-primary/TS-fallback/shadow behavior. SQL LIMIT alone is not a query-time bound. Do not fake cancelled after an uncontrolled scan or add a second SQLite owner.

Existing DB stores slug-prefixed file rows without snapshot identity; hash is 32 hex characters over possibly clipped text, coverage is not durable, and workspace reindex clears every row. Snapshot-aware metadata, atomic scoped reindex and serialized watch/manual writers require integration-owner patches in the same DB and a native parity decision before index status can claim exact coverage or restart-safe freshness.

CI-004 owns typed RPC/events/jobs and explicitly depends on CI-001/CI-002, not CI-003. Coordinate canonical search/read/cancel payloads and repository.index.changed/search.completed/search.cancelled events without inventing a new DAG edge. Headless CI-003 work can begin after its explicit dependencies, but production RC-07/RC-09 and authoritative UI/runtime receipts need the shared RPC/surface integration. Screenshots/ARIA/font proof remain required if the actual surface changes; do not mark UI acceptance N/A solely because the owned files are headless. Native agent transport readiness is additionally required when agent tools are exercised.

sharedPatchRequests.change: Accept the canonical authorized snapshot scope and bounded query controls; carry backend/error/truncation/coverage/index-revision receipts across TS and native branches. Expose metadata readback and scoped atomic reindex rather than importing storage internals from local-search.ts. Add native parity/cancellation only with a verified transport contract; otherwise report unsupported/unavailable explicitly, not a success simulation.
sharedPatchRequests.reason: Existing facade preserves primary/shadow/fallback semantics but accepts only workspaceRoot/query/limit, drops rich status, and cannot bind queries to a snapshot or cancellation budget.

sharedPatchRequests.change: Reuse the existing live watcher registry and opt-in feature flag. nextExecutableAction: Lead first commits wave0 and accepts CI-001/CI-002 artifact plus readback receipts. Then rehash inspected source on the approved committed handoff, resolve manifest lineage and shared-file leases, obtain canonical CodeSearchProvider/scope/error/cancellation schemas, and agree facade snapshot/coverage/native-parity patches. Implement only the three normative CI-003 new files in dependency order; integration owner applies shared requests and performs the exact runtime, negative-control, restart and relevant surface proof. This preflight is not a prerequisite implementation receipt.
risks: Root integration may change working-tree refs/provider/source seams; these hashes describe inspected bytes only and must be revalidated at implementation handoff.
Synchronous SQLite plus facade-native fallback means cancellation and actual backend errors cannot be solved by an AbortSignal check around a Promise alone.
Workspace-wide FTS rows, pre-ranking scope filtering and full-index deletion can leak metadata or erase unrelated sources unless the shared index integration is snapshot-aware and scoped.
Existing per-root file/byte limits, silent body clipping, shortened body hash and limited-hit totals can falsely imply complete repository coverage or exact source hashes.
Watcher-off, root-cap/watch failure and overlapping flushes leave stale/racing indexes; per-read current policy and exact content receipts remain mandatory.
rg JSON byte offsets, Unicode, CRLF and trailing newline require explicit span/column semantics; rg zero-match exit must not be confused with malformed regex/process failure.
Running rg against live mutable roots breaks immutable dirty/historical snapshot semantics; temporary materialization must contain only approved bytes and be cleaned on cancellation.
The inspected symbol bridge drops dirty files lacking commitSha; adapter/explainer changes need canonical working-copy provenance rather than invented commit aliases.
The requested CodeSearchProvider methods are not defined in the inspected provider module; unilateral interfaces or provider registration would create a second convention.

CI-003 full contract includes permissions, persistence, events and RC-07/RC-09 receipts beyond its five literal DoD strings. Headless implementation alone cannot close production integration acceptance.
Existing tests were inspected, not executed; test titles and source manifests are not runtime/provider readiness evidence.
